It is completely normal to feel nervous or unsure about physical intimacy, and the idea that everyone "just knows" what to do is a common myth. In reality, healthy intimacy is something people learn through communication, practice, and paying attention to their partner. 

Because everyone has different comfort levels, boundaries, and preferences, there is no single "instruction manual" that works for every relationship. However, there are highly respected, safe, and educational resources designed specifically for teens to help you navigate relationships, consent, and physical intimacy step-by-step.

Here are some of the best online guides and resources:

### 1. Scarleteen
[Scarleteen](https://www.scarleteen.com/) is widely considered the gold standard for relationship and sexual education for teens and young adults. It is inclusive, non-judgmental, and highly detailed.
*   **What to look for:** 
    *   **[Ready or Not? The Scarleteen Sex Readiness Checklist](https://www.scarleteen.com/read/relationships/ready-or-not-scarleteen-sex-readiness-checklist):** A great starting point to help you and your partner figure out what you are ready for.
    *   **[First Times](https://www.scarleteen.com/read/sexuality-sexual-health/first-times-user-guide):** A guide that demystifies first-time physical experiences and helps lower anxiety.
    *   They also have guides on kissing, manual sex (fingering/handjobs), and oral sex, focusing on anatomy, technique, and communication.

### 2. Planned Parenthood (Info for Teens)
[Planned Parenthood's Teen Section](https://www.plannedparenthood.org/learn/teens) offers straightforward, medically accurate, and easy-to-read information about bodies, relationships, and sex.
*   **What to look for:**
    *   **[Relationships Section](https://www.plannedparenthood.org/learn/teens/relationships):** Guides on how to know if a relationship is healthy and how to talk to your partner.
    *   **[Sex & Sexuality](https://www.plannedparenthood.org/learn/teens/sex):** Clear explanations of different physical activities, how they work, and how to stay safe (including birth control and STI prevention).

### 3. Love is Respect
[Love is Respect](https://www.loveisrespect.org/) focuses on the emotional and relational side of intimacy, which is just as important as the physical side.
*   **What to look for:**
    *   **[Consent Guides](https://www.loveisrespect.org/resources/what-is-consent/):** Understanding how to ask for consent and how to read your partner's cues. This is the most important step to ensure neither of you feels pressured or uncomfortable.

### 4. Amaze
[Amaze.org](https://amaze.org/) uses short, animated videos to explain topics like puberty, relationships, consent, and sexual health in a highly accessible way. It is a great resource if you prefer watching or listening over reading long articles.
